title: Breviculus Collationis cum Donatistis
author: Augustine

passages.original: huius ergo auctoritate oppressi Donatistae cum de prophetis et domino Christo et apostolis aliquid dixissent ad hoc tamen, non tolerandos in ecclesia permixtos malos, de episcopis omnino nihil dicere uoluerunt. et tamen etiam de Iuda traditore et de his, quos Paulus tolerauit per inuidiam Christum annuntiantes, ipse Cyprianus sic intellexit, sic scripsit, quemadmodum ea catholici in suo mandato posuerunt, quod et dominus ludam ad exemplum malorum in ecclesia tolerandorum pertulerit et Paulus eos, de quibus talia dixit, non extra, sed intra ecclesiam sustinuerit.
passages.english: So the Donatists, pressed hard by his authority, though they had said something about the prophets and the Lord Christ and the apostles in support of this point, that bad men mixed in the church are not to be tolerated, were unwilling to say anything at all about the bishops. And yet concerning Judas the betrayer too, and concerning those whom Paul tolerated as they proclaimed Christ out of envy, Cyprian himself understood and wrote just as the catholics set these things down in their mandate: that the Lord bore with Judas as an example of bad men to be tolerated in the church, and that Paul put up with those of whom he said such things not outside but inside the church.
passages.notes: 'ludam' is a scanning error for 'Iudam' (Judas). 'His authority' refers to Cyprian (see context). 'Mandate' (mandatum) is the catholics' formal written brief submitted at the Conference.
